title: Reorder Data in Log Files
summary: Given an array of logs where each log is a space-delimited string and the first word is an identifier, reorder the logs so that all letter-logs come before any digit-logs.
statement: Given an array of logs where each log is a space-delimited string and the first word is an identifier, reorder the logs so that all letter-logs come before any digit-logs. Letter-logs should be sorted first by their content in lexicographical order, and if the contents are identical, by their identifiers in lexicographical order. Digit-logs should maintain their original order. Return the logs in the new order.
constraints: Letter-logs sort by content then identifier; digit-logs retain input order after all letter-logs.
Return the reordered complete log strings.
hints: Digit-log order is stable; only letter logs receive sort keys.
Separate the two kinds while scanning.
Sort letter triples by (body,identifier), then append untouched digit logs.
The tuple key exactly implements both letter tie rules and separation preserves digit order.
editorial: The tuple key exactly implements both letter tie rules and separation preserves digit order.

tests.explanation: Letter logs sort by body, then the two digit logs keep their original order.
The act and off letter bodies sort before the stable digit logs.
